newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear tire, union agree to 6-year labor pact.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear tire, union agree to 6-year labor pact.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. and the United Steelworkers of America have agreed on a new labour contract that could end a two-week-old strike by nearly 13,000 workers at one of the nation's largest tire makers.

"Goodyear receives the stability that comes with a six-year contract, the first long-term agreement in the history of master contract bargaining in the rubber industry," Jim Warren, spokesman for Akron, Ohio-based Goodyear, said on Saturday after the agreement was reached.
Details of the pact were not announced, but the steelworkers union, which represents the rubber workers, said it meets their objectives. Ratification votes were set for this week.

"The proposed agreement provides improvements in wages and benefits and addresses the employment involvement issues among others that we had identifed as important," said Dick Davis, a union spokesman.

Part of the agreement would also coordinate contract expiration dates for workers at three plants operated by Goodyear's Kelly-Springfield division and governed by separate agreements, the union and the company said.

Nearly 13,000 Goodyear workers went on strike on April 20 after negotiators were unable to reach agreement on a new contract. The negotiators had been in discussions for two months on neutral turf in a Cincinnati hotel.
The strike was the first to hit Goodyear since a 140-day work stoppage that paralysed the tire industry in 1976.

On April 1, Goodyear was chosen by the union as its target to set the pattern for 1997 bargaining with the industry in advance of the expiration of Goodyear's three-year labour contract reached in 1994.

Although pattern bargaining was in effect, union workers at Goodyear's largest competitor, Bridgestone Corp., have a contract that extends for another three years. That contract emerged from a lengthy and bitter 1994 strike during which the company used replacement workers and imported tires. The long strike drained the United Rubber Workers' strike fund, leading that union to join the steelworkers.
Contract discussions at Uniroyal Goodrich Tire Manufacturing Co., the third of the tire industry's so-called Big Three, recently recessed to await the outcome of the Goodyear talks.

The 13,000 striking employees worked at nine plants in Akron, Ohio, Gadsden, Ala., St. Marys, Ohio, Lincoln, Neb., Topeka, Kansas, Danville, Va., Marysville, Ohio, Union City, Tenn., and Sun Prairie, Wis.
Goodyear employs 91,000 people 45 plants in the United States and dozens more around the world.

The three Kelly-Springfield plants also involved in the new agreement are in Fayetteville, N.C., Tyler, Tex., and Freeport, Ill. About 2,100 workers at the Fayetteville plant went on strike April 22 over a separate contract.
Kelly-Springfield could not be reached for comment.
